title: Priority-weighted eviction and quota-fallback for fair burst handling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a priority-weighted eviction + quota-fallback mechanism for the global limiter fabric to (1) maintain SLOs during short bursts, (2) enforce fairness across tenants with different priority classes, and (3) provide graceful degraded behavior when limiter control-plane or regional token stores are partially unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: New eviction policy implemented in limiter that uses weight-based token buckets per priority class
When regional kv-store is read-only, requests are routed to local fast-path with degraded token accounting and documented conservative fallback ratios
Benchmarks show <=5% increase in tail latency for P0 requests under 10x burst compared to baseline and <=15% traffic loss for P2 under overload scenarios
Automated chaos test that kills limiter leader in a region results in <1.5x error spike and system recovers within configurable grace window
Config flags allow operator to toggle 'strict fairness' vs 'latency-first' modes without deploy rollback
implementation_notes: Use existing token-bucket shards; attach 'priority_weight' metadata to tenant tokens to compute eviction ordering
Eviction decision: prefer evicting from lowest priority candidates with highest recent burst ratio and lowest observed SLO contribution
Fallback mode: if lease to central quota store times out, switch to local conservative quotas derived from last-known state and a decay window
Expose metrics: evictions_total, fallback_activations, fairness_ratio_by_priority, fallback_duration_seconds
Plan requires a small schema change in quota lease (versioned) and graceful migration strategy
tasks: Prototype eviction comparator function and unit tests (ENG)
Add 'priority_weight' to tenant registration flow (API) and update SDK docs (DX)
Implement local fallback token accounting and decay algorithm
Integrate with rollout framework for canary and A/B toggles
End-to-end chaos test covering regional leader failover and kv-store latency spikes
Create dashboard and alert rules; wire to oncall runbook
risks: Mis-tuned weights could starve lower tiers during sustained bursts (mitigation: conservative defaults + operator override)
Increased complexity in eviction logic may add CPU cost on limiter hot path (mitigation: micro-benchmarks and native fast-path optimizations)
Schema migration for quota leases could cause transient mis-accounting if older servers remain in fleet (mitigation: feature-flagged rollout and compatibility layer)
Fallback conservative quotas may be too restrictive for some enterprise customers — include per-customer opt-outs for Dedicated customers
rollback_plan: Feature gate the new eviction policy. If we observe >2x error rate for P0 or unexplained fairness regressions during canary, flip gate off and revert only the gate binding (no full deploy rollback required). Have DB migration reversal script available to restore previous lease format within 30 minutes.
monitoring: Create 'limiter/eviction/decision_time_ms' histogram and alert on >99th percentile >10ms
Alert if fairness_ratio_by_priority deviates >30% from baseline for more than 5 minutes
Track fallback_activations and correlate with region-leader-heartbeats metric
SLO dashboards: request success rate by priority (P0,P1,P2), p95/p99 latencies, and token-accounting drift
qa_plan: Unit tests for eviction ordering and weight math
Integration tests with local quota-store emulator
Load test with mixed-priority synthetic tenants using limiter-sim (simulate 10k tenants across 3 regions)
Chaos test: kill regional limiter leader and kv-store process repeatedly while measuring SLO impact
deploy_plan: Deploy feature-gated limiter binary to canary cluster (5% traffic) for 24h
Run automated load suite and monitor fairness and P0 latency
If metrics are stable, enable default weights; otherwise, revert gate and iterate on tuning
comments: 2025-11-13 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Decided to prioritize local fallback behavior over trying to synchronously repair remote stores during short bursts.
2025-11-18 — Liam O'Connor: Prototype comparator implemented. Microbenchmarks show comparator adds ~0.8us per decision; acceptable but will optimize native code path.
2025-11-21 — Mei Chen (SRE): Reviewed metrics plan. Recommend adding 'eviction_reason' tag for better post-incident analysis. Added to implementation notes.
2025-11-25 — PR #1423 opened for initial API and weight plumbing. Requesting review from runtime team and security for schema change.
2025-11-29 — Performance lab: 10x burst test across 3 regions. Observed 9% tail latency increase for P1, P0 stayed within 3% of baseline. Logged traces to help optimize hot path.
2025-12-01 — Product review (Anika Gomez): PM OK with conservative defaults; asked for a customer-facing config to opt into 'latency-first' mode. Added as follow-up task.
2025-12-03 — Liam O'Connor: Started chaos test harness integration. Identified one race when lease expiry and eviction run coincide; created ENG-23147 to track race fix.
notes: This ticket focuses on short-burst scenarios (seconds to a couple minutes). Sustained overload is out of scope and will be handled by existing autoscaling + quota policies.
Keep design modular: eviction strategy should be pluggable so we can experiment with alternate fairness algorithms (proportional fairness, max-min fairness) without a full deploy.
In conversations with Legal, no additional compliance controls required for this change, but document retention of eviction logs for 90 days for auditability.
